title: Largest Subset with Minimum Pair Gap
statement:
You are given an array `arr` of `n` integers and an integer `y`. Choose a subset of the array elements (any elements, by index, not necessarily contiguous) such that the absolute difference between **every pair** of chosen elements is at least `y`.

Print the size of the largest such subset. A subset of one element always qualifies. Two equal elements have difference `0`, so they can both be chosen only when `y = 0`.
input_format:
The first line contains `n` and `y`.
The second line contains `n` integers: the array `arr`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the maximum size of a valid subset.

examples.explanation: Sorted, the array is -900 1 1 2 2 4 5 10 15 18 20 100 101. Taking -900, 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 100 keeps every consecutive gap at least 4 (the gaps are 901, 4, 5, 5, 5, 80). No subset of 8 exists.
All elements are equal, so any two have difference 0 which is below 3. Only one can be chosen.
Choose 0, 10 and 20. Adding any other element would put it within 5 of one of them.

hints: Only the gaps between neighbours in sorted order matter: if every consecutive pair of the chosen elements is far enough apart, then every pair is.
Sort the array, then decide greedily: always keep the smallest element, because starting as low as possible leaves the most room for later picks.
After the first pick, take the next element that is at least `y` larger than the last element you kept.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, y = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    a = sorted(int(x) for x in data[2:2 + n])
    cnt = 1
    last = a[0]
    for x in a[1:]:
        if x - last >= y:
            cnt += 1
            last = x
    print(cnt)

main()
